newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 29.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 29.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** Leader of former finance minister P. Chidambaram's party withholds decision on whether to join the new federal government

Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) chief G.K. Moopanar consults with party leaders in the southern city of Madras over the decision on whether to enter new Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's week-old government
** Gujral faces his first shock waves in office as pressure builds on the leader of his party to quit over a corruption case and leftwing allies denounced his budget

** The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) says it has decided to prosecute Laloo Prasad Yadav, president of Gujral's Janata Dal party and chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar, in a probe into the use of state funds
** Four left-wing parties in Gujral's coalition call for changes in the pathbreaking 1997/98 (April-March) budget, due to be taken up by parliament this week
The Left Front issues a statement calling for changes in the areas of insurance, taxes, divestment in state enterprises, public distribution, customs duties and excise duties

** Term lending institutions the Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) and Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) cut their minimum lending rates to 15.0 percent per annum from 16.5 percent, with effect from May 1
The cut in rates follows the easier monetary and credit policy for first half 1997/98 (April-March) announced by the Reserve Bank of India on April 15
** Indian officials, promising the new government would keep economic policies steady, say that India could double its annual $1.0 billion World Bank borrowing if the right projects could be found
** Electrical equipment maker Crompton Greaves says 1996/97 net profit falls to 307.6 million rupees, from 640.4 a year earlier
** Industrial Credit & Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) meeting to decide on a cut in its prime lending rate
** Sales of India's largest truckmaker Tata Engineering and Locomotive Company (TELCO) climb 19 percent during 1996/97, a source close to company says

He says TELCO's vehicle sales jump to 215,276 during the financial year ended March 31, 1997, from 181,200 a year earlier. Production during 1996/97 rises 20 percent to 218,393 units, from 181,401 in the previous year

** Asian Electronics approves an increase in foreign institutional investor (FII) holding in the company to 30 percent from 24 percent and decides to issue preferential shares worth $6 million to International Finance Corporation (IFC) at a price of "not less than 150 rupees per share."
** The board of Century Textiles and Industries Ltd will meet on May 6 to consider an issue of bonus equity shares
** Orchid Chemicals says its 1996/97 net rises to 306.5 million rupees, from 173.7 million a year earlier
** Exide Industries says its net profit climbs to 309.3 million rupees, in the year to March 31, 1997 from 204.1 million in the previous year
** ICICI raises 23 billion rupees through its retail debt issue which closed on Monday but the company is unlikely to exercise the full greenshoe option, the Financial Express newspaper says
MARKETS:
** Bombay's benchmark stocks index ended mostly unchanged on Monday as speculators awaited the return of the TMC to the government -- the index closed 0.06 points lower at 3825.51
-- Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
